_doc: T2.8 calibration corridors — every band is TUNE data (D-006). Two-sided by construction: the battery fails when a metric leaves its band in EITHER direction, and fails when the metric produced no signal at all (no-output-is-failure). Bands were measured on the T2.7b honest dynamics (ADR-011 kernel) and widened to cover seed variance, not to make tests pass: see each band's note.

canonical._doc: Canonical production autoplay (sim autoplay: 1024 px world, N = 12, 650 turns to year 4500). Fed-era corridors: at this scale the world is far below capacity for the whole horizon.

fedGrowthPerYear.note: The ratified T2.7 band 0.05-0.1 %/yr verbatim; measured 0.00072-0.00076 across seeds after the 800-year founding warm-up.

crudeBirthRatePer1000.note: Pre-modern CBR corridor around the measured 41.5; the historical envelope is ~30-55, the tune sits mid-range.

crudeDeathRatePer1000.note: CDR tracks CBR minus the growth band; measured 40.7.

pyramidChildShare.note: Measured 0.410; pre-modern high-fertility pyramids are 0.35-0.45 under-15.

pyramidElderShare.note: Measured 0.026 with the BandViews elder boundary; pre-modern survival past the elder line is rare.

densityPerArableKm2.note: People per fertility-weighted arable km2 at year 4500. BAND UNCHANGED AT T3.1 (floor briefly lowered to 0.12, REVERTED on director ruling: a historical corridor may not be loosened because the measured value moved). WHAT 'ARABLE' MEANS since T3.1: sum over lattice blocks INSIDE settlement catchments of (mean agronomic-suitability index) x (block km2). The moisture BFS now seeds from RIVERS as well as the sea, so interior river valleys score as suitable where they previously scored ~0 - the denominator's UNIT changed. Measured, same seed and horizon, pre vs post: population 115,627 -> 120,310 (+4.1%), arable 388,145 -> 809,711 km2 (x2.09), density 0.298 -> 0.149. The world did not get emptier; the denominator doubled. RE-DERIVATION (four reference classes, two adversarial reviews): the floor of 0.12 was NOT supported. Against capacity-denominated historical anchors - LBK Rhineland 0.42-0.44 p/km2 over the whole atlas region including empty forest (Zimmermann), Neolithic Britain 0.24-1.19 over the whole island, Illinois Territory 1810 at 0.12-0.17 as the emptiest documented sustained farming frontier - the sim's 0.0757-0.0784 per RAW catchment km2 is 1.6-2.2x emptier than the emptiest. The one comparison that passed (global habitable-land density 0.067 at 4000 BC / 0.135 at 3000 BC) mismatches denominators: it includes Siberia, Amazonia and every forager. THE WORLD THEREFORE STRADDLES THE FLOOR - measured 0.1415 (seed 7), 0.1468 (42), 0.1486 (1), 0.1630 (2), so three of four seeds are OUT OF CORRIDOR - and the deviation is escalated in docs/adr/cr-002.md rather than absorbed by moving this band. DIAGNOSIS: the metric is dominated by catchment GEOMETRY, not demography - the catchment radius is 205 km (41x the classic 5 km working radius, 51 hours' walk one way). At a 40 km radius the same population reads 3.9 per weighted km2, inside the settled-agrarian range. The derived floor from the correct class (frontier/unfilled agrarian: LBK Rhineland, Neolithic Britain, Maori NZ 1769, Anglo-American frontier 1790-1810; ceiling cross-checked against Boserup 1965 forest-fallow) is 0.25 with a ceiling of 2.30 - i.e. the honest band is ABOVE the standing one at both ends. The band is HELD at [0.15, 0.6] rather than raised, because raising it is also a change to the instrument and needs the same ruling. The old note's '~10-30/km2 of mature agrarian land use' justification is WITHDRAWN: those are worked-area densities and are not commensurable with an isochrone denominator.

migrationGrossPerDecade.note: Fraction of population moving per decade; measured 0.0004 in the fed era (famine flight, the big driver, is absent). Upper edge = the T2.5 rig corridor ceiling.

dev._doc: Dev-world autoplay (256 px, N = 4, 1000 turns): the capacity horizon is reachable, so the Malthus corridors live here.

crashCount.note: At least one >=20% boom-crash must occur (measured: exactly 1 per seed, first at t ~ 590-660); more than 3 in 1000 turns would be the oscillation pathology, not the Malthus cycle.

firstCrashTurn.note: RE-BANDED at T3.1 (was [400,800], measured 255-535 on M2 dynamics): the worldgen refresh moved it - river valleys are moist now (moisture BFS credits riverbanks), so catchment fertility and carrying capacity rose world-wide and the growth-to-overshoot arc lengthened. Measured on the refreshed dynamics: 806 (seed 7), 826 (seed 42); band covers seed variance with margin. T3.10 re-examines with the goods economy in place.

crashDepth.note: Measured 0.71-0.83 peak-to-trough; a <0.4 dip is a wobble not a crash, >0.95 is extinction.

postCrashPopulation.note: The survivors must oscillate around capacity (~10.2k measured 10.2-11.6k final), not die out and not re-boom past the peak.

starvationRatePer1000.note: Whole-run starvation deaths per 1000 person-years (measured 0.42-0.44): famine demography must EXIST (zero means the crash was bloodless = dodge regression) and must not dominate base mortality.

migrationGrossPerDecade.note: Measured 0.0013-0.0029; famine flight around the crash lifts the dev world above the fed canonical rate.
